newsitem.title: USA: Details of Archer's five-year tax relief plan.
newsitem.headline: Details of Archer's five-year tax relief plan.

text.p: The chairman of the House Ways and Means Committee, Representative Bill Archer, Monday unveiled his proposal to cut taxes by a net $84.6 billion through 2002 and $249.7 billion through 2007.
The 10-year tax cut would be partially offset by $47 billion in higher revenue paid to the government through 2002 and $109.2 billion paid through 2007.
The major components of the Texas Republican's tax proposal are as follows, all in calendar years. The estimates were made by the House and Senate Joint Committee on Taxation.

-- Child care tax credit for children under age 17, $400 in 1998 and $500 thereafter, phased out at $110,000 per couple adjusted gross income. Total tax cut $71.3 billion to 2002, $149.5 billion through 2007. Archer said this will cover 41 million children.

-- Capital gains tax rate cut to 20 percent from 28 percent maximum with indexing for inflation to start in 2001 and effective for gains realised after May 7, 1997. It raises $2.6 billion in revenue through 2002 and cuts taxes by $35 billion through 2007.
-- Repeal of capital gains tax on the first $500,000 of income from sale of principal home for a couple, $250,000 for an individual. This tax break currently available only for those 55 and over.
-- Corporate capital gains held five years, now 35 percent, taxed at 32 percent in 1998, 31 percent in 1999 and 30 percent thereafter.

-- Education tax credits worth $31 billion through 2002, and $75.5 billion through 2007. HOPE scholarship tax credit worth 50 percent of tuition and book expenses up to $3,000. Phased out at joint incomes of $80,000-$100,000. Deduction of up to $10,000 per student per year for prepaid tuition programmes. Penalty-free withdrawals from Individual Retirement Accounts for college and graduate education. Permits parents to make tax-free contributions to education investment account for child under age 18.
-- Creation of non-deductible Individual Retirement Accounts, to be called "American Dream" savings accounts, deposits would be from taxable income but earnings could be withdrawn tax-free.

-- Various changes in the estate tax provisions including an incremental increase in the estate and gift tax credit to $1 million by $20,000 per year through 2002 and $25,000 per year thereafter. Estate tax indexed for inflation. Tax cut of $3.1 billion through 2002 and $19 billion through 2007.
The Archer tax proposal also seeks to raise $47.1 billion through 2002 and $109.2 billion through 2007 by extensions of various taxes and curbs on other tax breaks.

-- Airline ticket tax extended at a lower 7.5 percent rate, down from the current 10 percent of ticket price. An additional tax would be imposed of $2 per flight segment starting Oct. 1, and rising to $3 in 2002 with annual inflation increases. An additional tax of 7.5 percent would be imposed on payments to airlines for travel under credit card and similar programmes. These taxes would raise $27.3 billion through 2002 and $65.8 billion through 2007.

-- International departure fees would be increased to $10 per passenger. Arrivals would also be charged the same fee and both would be indexed to increase with inflation. This would raise $4.1 billion through 2002, $10.2 billion through 2007.
-- Federal income tax imposed on income earned by Indian tribes on gaming or other businesses. Raises $1.9 billion through 2002 and $4.5 billion through 2007.
-- Tightens rules on taxation of company-paid life insurance to raise $1.2 billion through 2002, $2.2 billion through 2007.
Two other important, but more arcane, tax rules would be revised.

-- Phase-out of the coporate alternative minimum tax, a tax enacted to make sure that all companies pay some tax despite hefty deductions. Full repeal in 2006. Tax cut worth $17 billion through 2002 and $34 billion through 2007.
-- Increase the alternative minimum tax exemption for individuals by $1,000 every other year through 2007 with tax cut worth $1.3 billion through 2002 and $15.4 billion through 2007.
